topic: Using Standard Library Algorithms with Iterators
explanation: In modern C++, the Standard Template Library (STL) provides a rich set of algorithms that operate on containers via iterators. This approach promotes generic programming, code reuse, and efficiency. By passing iterators to algorithms like 'swap_ranges', programmers can perform complex operations on various container types without rewriting code for each container. This concept emphasizes the power of iterator-based algorithms to manipulate data structures seamlessly and efficiently within the C++ language.
syntax:
template <class InputIt1, class InputIt2> 
InputIt2 swap_ranges(InputIt1 first1, InputIt1 last1, InputIt2 first2);
code_example: // Swap first four elements of coll1 with first four elements of coll2
for (const auto& elem : coll1) std::cout << elem << ' ';
for (const auto& elem : coll2) std::cout << elem << ' ';
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of the 'swap_ranges' algorithm from the STL, which swaps elements between two ranges specified by iterators. It swaps the first four elements of a vector with the first four elements of a deque, showcasing how algorithms operate generically on different container types through iterators. The code highlights modern C++ practices by using range-based containers, iterator-based algorithms, and clean, expressive syntax to manipulate data efficiently.
